chunk_findings.detail: The task `P2.T4b` is explicitly narrowed to `globs="ledger/report/format.py"`, but the immediately following `work` call for `P2.T4b` writes `{"ledger/report/format.py": FORMAT_PY, "tests/test_summary.py": SUMMARY_TEST}`. Since the scenario treats task globs as the set of files the task may touch (for example, `P2.T5` is given globs that include both `ledger/report/csv_export.py` and `tests/test_csv.py`), completing `P2.T4b` modifies `tests/test_summary.py` outside the declared globs. If ddflow’s glob guardrails are enforced, this completion fails; if not, the task metadata is still wrong and records an out-of-scope change.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_change.py:act5_requirements_change_mid_flight

chunk_findings.detail: The deletion loop intentionally preserves anything under `.ddflow` (`if ".ddflow" not in path.parts and ".git" not in path.parts`), but the subsequent “code is genuinely gone” assertion only excludes `.git`: `remaining = [p for p in repo.rglob("*.py") if ".git" not in p.parts]`. If the demo repository has any surviving Python file under `.ddflow` (for example `.ddflow/hook.py` or another log/tool artifact), that file is not deleted by the loop but is included in `remaining`, so `sc.check("the code is genuinely gone", not remaining, ...)` fails even though no source file outside `.ddflow` remains. The check should mirror the deletion filter by also excluding `.ddflow`, or the deletion loop should not preserve `.ddflow` Python files if they are meant to be deleted.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_finish.py:122

chunk_findings.detail: `Entry.total()` starts the sum with `Money(0)`, which hard-codes USD. Since `Money` explicitly supports other currencies and `Posting` does not restrict the entry to USD, a balanced EUR entry fails: `Entry("x", [Posting(Account("1000", "Cash", "asset"), Money(100, "EUR")), Posting(Account("2000", "Payable", "liability"), Money(-100, "EUR"))]).total()` raises `ValueError: cannot add USD to EUR` at the first addition. The same input makes `validate(entry)` raise a `ValueError` from `Money.__add__` rather than returning `True`, even though `VALIDATE_PY` itself expects zero to be constructed in the first posting’s currency.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_data.py:ENTRY_PY

chunk_findings.detail: The scenario check for the brief is tautological: `"D1" in brief or True` is always true in Python. Given any `ddflow_brief` result that omits the required decision marker `D1` (for example, an empty brief or a brief containing only unrelated decisions), `work` still reports `"{item}'s brief carries the rules and decisions in force"` as passed. This makes the scenario’s guardrail assertion meaningless and allows a missing/incorrect brief to pass silently.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: The moved per-task helper `work` still contains the assertion `sc.check(f"{item}'s brief carries the rules and decisions in force", "D1" in brief or True, "")`. The `or True` makes the checked condition always true, so the check passes even when the returned brief does not mention `D1` or any decisions/rules in force. For example, if `ddflow_brief` for `P1.T1` returns a brief that omits `D1`, this split code still reports that the brief “carries the rules and decisions in force” as passed, hiding a real regression in brief content.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:work

chunk_findings.detail: In `act4_close_the_phase`, the loop records gate `docs` as `outcome="passed"` with evidence `"README documents Money, Account, Entry and validate"` (line 75), then immediately calls `ddflow_gate_skip` for the same `docs` gate and asserts `code == 0` (line 85). The same gate is marked both passed and skipped, and the recorded evidence is fabricated because the later skip reason says documentation is out of scope. On a correct ddflow implementation, skipping an already-passed gate should fail, making the line 85 check fail; on a lax implementation, the demo passes while falsely reporting that `docs` was explicitly skipped. The `docs` entry must not be recorded as passed in the loop if it is meant to be skipped.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_change.py:75,85

chunk_findings.detail: The `remaining` list used in the “code is genuinely gone” check excludes only `.git`, while the deletion loop at line 120 deliberately spares files whose path contains `.ddflow` (`if ".ddflow" not in path.parts and ".git" not in path.parts`). If `.ddflow/` contains any Python file (for example a hook or plugin stored in `.ddflow/`), that file is left on disk by design, but then appears in `remaining`, causing the check to fail even though the recorded step says only `.ddflow/` survives. The filter should also exclude `.ddflow` to match the deletion policy.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_finish.py:122

chunk_findings.detail: `Entry.total` initializes the accumulator as `Money(0)`, which defaults to `"USD"`. For a valid single-currency entry not in USD, e.g. `Entry("sale", [Posting(cash, Money(100, "EUR")), Posting(cash, Money(-100, "EUR"))]).total()`, the first addition `Money(0) + Money(100, "EUR")` raises `ValueError: cannot add USD to EUR` instead of returning `Money(0, "EUR")`. The same issue makes `validate` raise `ValueError` for balanced non-USD entries, so the money model supports currencies its journal entry model cannot actually use.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_data.py:ENTRY_PY:Entry.total

chunk_findings.detail: The check `"D1" in brief or True` is always `True`, so `sc.check` can never fail. Given an input where `client.tool("ddflow_brief", item=item)[0]` returns a brief that does not contain `"D1"` (for example an empty string or unrelated text), the scenario still claims the brief carries the rules and decisions in force, which is wrong because the check is vacuous.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: The old module-level `_BETA = [None]` was deleted in this diff, but the replacement import is for `BETA` (no leading underscore). The retained `act1_the_operator_speaks` in the same file still refers to `_BETA`, so running the demo reaches that assignment and raises `NameError: name '_BETA' is not defined`. The diff does not update that reference to `BETA`.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_acts_run_in_the_same_order` uses `ast.walk(run)` to collect act-call names and then asserts an exact order. Python documents `ast.walk` as yielding nodes “in no specified order”, so a different Python implementation or a future CPython traversal change can make the collected calls come out in a different order even when `scenario_full_lifecycle.py` still runs the acts in the correct order. That would make this test fail on a correct split; the check should traverse the ordered statement list/body nodes instead of relying on `ast.walk` ordering.

chunk_findings.detail: The scenario claims to verify that the umbrella task’s gates were rolled up by checking only that the `ddflow_gate_status` text does not contain `"never run"`, but it ignores the call’s exit code (`code`). If `ddflow_gate_status` fails for any reason other than a literal `"never run"` message — for example, it returns `(text="unknown item: P1.T3", code=2)` or an internal-error message — the `sc.check` still passes because `"never run"` is absent. That makes the demo falsely report that no gate of the umbrella is left silent even though the gate status was never successfully obtained.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_build.py:203

chunk_findings.detail:
In `act8_rebuild_from_the_log`, the deletion loop deliberately preserves every `.py` file under `.ddflow` because that directory is the surviving log, but the subsequent check for “the code is genuinely gone” filters out only `.git`:

```python
if ".ddflow" not in path.parts and ".git" not in path.parts:
    path.unlink()
remaining = [p for p in repo.rglob("*.py") if ".git" not in p.parts]
```

If the repository contains any Python file under `.ddflow` that is not part of the removed `.ddflow/worktrees` tree — for example `.ddflow/ddflow.py`, `.ddflow/hooks/pre_commit.py`, or another vendored script — that file is intentionally left in place, then appears in `remaining`, and `sc.check("the code is genuinely gone", not remaining, ...)` fails. The check should exclude `.ddflow` as well, or it falsely reports that source code survived when only the log was supposed to survive.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_finish.py:119

chunk_findings.detail:
`FORMAT_PY` is a plain triple-quoted string, but its body contains `return "
".join(lines)` with a single backslash. When `lifecycle_data.py` is imported, Python interprets that `
` as a real newline, so the constant contains an unterminated string literal: `return "` followed by a newline, then `".join(lines)`. If the scenario writes `FORMAT_PY` to `ledger/report/format.py` and then imports it (as `SUMMARY_TEST` does via `from ledger.report.format import render`), the generated module raises `SyntaxError: unterminated string literal`. The same single-backslash escaping bug appears in `CSV_PY` (`lineterminator="
"`), producing the same failure when `ledger/report/csv_export.py` is generated and imported by `CSV_TEST`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_data.py:FORMAT_PY

chunk_findings.detail: The condition `"D1" in brief or True` is always true because Python evaluates it as `("D1" in brief) or True`. Therefore `sc.check(... "brief carries the rules and decisions in force" ...)` passes even when `ddflow_brief` returns a brief that does not contain `D1`, e.g. `"no decisions in force"`. The check gives a false pass and cannot detect a broken or empty brief.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: The function records `gate="merge", outcome="passed"` before actually calling `ddflow_merge`, and it never checks the merge result. If `ddflow_merge` fails, for example because of a merge conflict or an invalid worktree, the gate history has already been written as a successful merge; `ddflow_complete` is then called and may rely on that false gate, or at minimum the task’s audit trail falsely claims the merge gate passed.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:96

chunk_findings.detail: This test claims to verify that the acts “run in the same order,” but it only walks the entire AST of `run` and accepts any `act*` call anywhere in the function, including calls inside nested function bodies that may never be executed. For example, if `scenario_full_lifecycle.run` contains `def _unused(): act1_the_operator_speaks()` before top-level calls to `act2_phase_one_in_parallel()` through `act8_rebuild_from_the_log()`, the collected call list still equals the expected eight names and the test passes, even though invoking `run()` never executes `act1_the_operator_speaks`. Thus the test can pass despite a behavioural regression in the moved code.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_scenario_lifecycle_split.py:test_acts_run_in_the_same_order

chunk_findings.detail: The check claims to verify that a bug with no regression test cannot be closed, but the preceding call `alpha.tool("ddflow_bug_fixed", id="B1")` runs before B1 is ever recorded (the only `B1` record in this file is the later `bug_hunt` gate evidence). Since `ddflow_bug_fixed` can return a non-zero exit for an unknown bug id, `code != 0` passes even if ddflow’s no-regression-test guard is broken; the scenario does not actually exercise the behavior named in the step.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_build.py:170

chunk_findings.detail: The full-suite run is hardcoded to `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`. In an environment where `python3` is not on PATH (for example Windows, where the launcher is `python`) or where `python3` refers to a different interpreter than the one running the demo (no project dependencies installed), `ddflow ci run` fails and act4 cannot close P1. The immediately preceding live-run block at the same act uses `sys.executable`; this call should do the same instead of assuming `python3`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_change.py:88

chunk_findings.detail: The check “no finding names a removed item” only tests `f["item"].startswith("X.")`, but the removed phase `PX` is also a removed item. If `ddflow_loops` returns `[{"item": "PX", "kind": "..."}]` after `PX` was removed, the comprehension filters it out because `"PX".startswith("X.")` is `False`, so the asserted condition is `True` and the scenario passes despite a finding naming the removed phase. The check should include `"PX"` or otherwise test against all removed ids, not only the `X.*` task ids.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_finish.py:55

chunk_findings.detail: The generated `Entry.total` initializes the accumulator as `Money(0)`, which has the default currency `"USD"`. A valid non-USD journal entry therefore crashes before balancing: `Entry("sale", [Posting(Account("1000", "Cash", "asset"), Money(100, "EUR")), Posting(Account("4000", "Sales", "revenue"), Money(-100, "EUR"))]).total()` raises `ValueError: cannot add USD to EUR`. This is wrong because `Money` and `VALIDATE_PY.validate` explicitly support non-USD currencies (`validate` uses `entry.postings[0].amount.currency`), but `Entry.total` makes every non-USD entry unusable.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_data.py:ENTRY_PY `Entry.total`

chunk_findings.detail: The condition `"D1" in brief or True` is always `True`, so `sc.check` can never fail here. If `ddflow_brief` returns a brief that does not contain the required rule `"D1"` (for example `brief = "no rules"`), the task still passes the "brief carries the rules and decisions in force" check and proceeds to implement and merge, when the stated assertion should have stopped it.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: The moved `_work` helper still contains `sc.check(f"{item}'s brief carries the rules and decisions in force", "D1" in brief or True, "")`. The `or True` makes the check unconditionally true: if `ddflow_brief` returns `"No decisions in force"`, the scenario still passes and continues as though decision `D1` applies, so the lifecycle no longer actually catches a ddflow regression where the brief omits the rules and decisions in force.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:work

chunk_findings.detail: The moved `_act8_rebuild_from_the_log` computes `remaining = [p for p in repo.rglob("*.py") if ".git" not in path.parts]`, using `path` left over from the preceding deletion loop rather than the comprehension variable `p`. That makes the predicate a single constant per call. If the repository has a Python file under `.git`, such as `.git/hooks/pre-commit.py`, the deletion loop leaves it in place, but `path` is the last project file outside `.git`, so the stale predicate is true for every remaining file and the hook appears in `remaining`; `sc.check("the code is genuinely gone", not remaining, ...)` then fails even though no project source code remains. The predicate should be `.git not in p.parts`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_acts_finish.py:act8_rebuild_from_the_log
